summary: What a page may call on window.SF. A public name keeps its meaning and is renamed or removed only through the change journal, as an attribute is; an internal one is the runtime's and may change in any release. tests/browser/public-js-api.browser.mjs holds the list against the runtime: every name the runtime puts on window.SF is here, and every public name and member the probe loads is there. A component's script API (SF.Input, SF.Carousel, ...) arrives with its component and is listed with it; tests/browser/public-js-api-components.browser.mjs loads every Smart tag on one page, and the plain components with a script API on a second, and holds those names' members the same way. loaded_by says when a name exists: core -- as soon as core.js has run, before the next script on the page; core-loader -- when the Loader has started, at the window event sf-loader-init (core.js loads it); smart-base -- when the Smart base has loaded (SF.loadSmartBase(), or the first Smart element on the page); component/<name>, smart/<name> -- with that component. The probe takes the names at each of those moments (documentation trial 6, 2026-10-18: the Loader's names were listed under core). layer and audience say where the documentation lists a name (owner decision D17, 2026-11-11): layer is core, loader, smart-base or component -- the documentation's Functions section lists the Framework's own names grouped by the first three, and a component's script API (layer component) is documented on its component's page; audience is public (listed for authors) or internal (not listed). Both are derived from loaded_by and status by scripts/generate-public-js-api-layers.mjs, whose exception table says why a name differs. author is the one line the documentation shows for a name (one sentence, present tense, no history), and doc, when there is one, the slug of the page that describes it (language-neutral, an anchor after #); both are written by hand. summary is the release's record of what the name does. public-js-api.schema.json is the shape.

globals.name: SF.Loader
globals.author: Loads the components and utilities a page uses on demand and follows parts added to the page.
globals.summary: The runtime loader: loads what a page uses, components and utilities, on demand, and the theme. ensure(tags, {timeout}) asks for elements and settles with {ready, missing}, never rejecting; watch(root) marks a box an element renders into as a portal the Loader reads as the page (unwatch unmarks it). Once a theme is set (setTheme, changeTheme), SF.Loader.theme and SF.Loader.themePreference read it. checkTheme() applies the saved or the system theme again (a page that swaps its document calls it). ComponentRegistry holds the classes of the scripted components by name (ComponentRegistry.Modal).

globals.name: SF.RuleLoader
globals.author: Holds the load rules by name and registers a component set's rules and exports.
globals.open_members: Its enumerable keys are the load rules by name (a class, a tag, a component); registerPackage and packageOf are functions, not rules, and are not enumerated.
globals.summary: The load rules by name: what a class, a tag or a component needs. A component set adds its own rules here (its rule.js) with SF.RuleLoader.registerPackage(name, {rules, api, aliases, exports, base}); SF.RuleLoader.packageOf(name) answers where a set is served ({name, base, declared, registered, version, release, api, exported}, frozen). Both are functions, not rules, and are not enumerated.

The events sf-workspace-view {view} and sf-workspace-panel {open} fire on the element (docs/developer/workspace-layout.md).

globals.name: SF.Composition

A page and the documentation also call validate(document, registry) (the problems of a document against its types), normalize(document, registry) (the document with its defaults written out), render(document, context) (the document drawn as elements), resolveRecipe(recipe, context) and parseRecipeJson(text) with Recipe (a composition recipe read and resolved into a document), startInlineEdit(element, options) (inline text editing, once sf-editor-inline is loaded), compositionTypeFromSmartManifest(manifest) (a composition type from a Smart manifest), and the tables FRAGMENT_DESCRIPTOR_SCHEMA (the fragment descriptor's schema id), BUILTIN_TYPE_MANIFESTS (the built-in types) and VALUE_TYPES (the port value types).

globals.name: SF.copyFeedback

globals.name: SF.ready
globals.author: Waits for the Loader to start, as a promise or with a callback.
globals.summary: The Loader's readiness (simai/ui-source#16), on window.SF as soon as core.js has run. A thenable: await SF.ready (or SF.ready.then) settles with window.SF exactly when the Loader sends sf-loader-init -- SF.Loader, SF.loadSmartBase and the other core-loader names are there by then -- and a script that asks later gets it already settled; it never rejects. One per page: created once on the shared global, kept by every later bundle (a second core.js included) and never replaced. Called as SF.ready(fn), it runs fn once the Loader is up and the document has been parsed, synchronously when both have happened. A script that runs before core.js queues a function with (window.SF_ON_READY = window.SF_ON_READY || []).push(fn); fn is called with window.SF at the same moment.
